title: Prove sharp signed tensor gap with variable target boundaries (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with finite exact corroboration: variable productive boundaries can strictly improve a normalized signed tensor-frame invoice. This package determines the exact optimum and threshold for one explicit abstract graph, rather than treating failure of an averaging argument as a construction.

```text
J_t = sum_i dim(S_i)^t - sum_(i<j) d(S_i,S_j)^t
min J_1 in K^m = -floor(3m/2), over every field K
min J_t / 2^t at m=2 = min(-1, 3/2^t - 3)
one-copy optimum = -1; strict coupling advantage iff 2^t > 3/2
```

Every linear minimizer is classified: the spaces are pairwise disjoint and have balanced dimensions. The proof constructs attaining graph subspaces over every field. At the linear tariff, two copies improve the normalized value from -1 to -3/2. This is a scoped rank-graph result, not a legal scalar word, supplier, complete multiplication theorem or new kappa.

The new result addresses the variable-boundary limitation and second open question of Ali Romman's [PR6171](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6171), at `343232cdf5273d1f77569de390f0977b46916644`. It goes beyond that package's arithmetic negative-credit control by proving an exact attainable graph optimum, equality cases and power threshold. Its fixed-boundary theorem is cited, not audited or replayed. Cinna Davis retains the projection inequality and icekylinx the subspace-frame construction; all P104/native/helper/caller/compiler predecessor credit is retained. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Standard dimension and affine-envelope facts are background; no literature-priority claim.

Package: `research/signed-triangle-tensor-gap/`. Base main `3f0152a32eeebac0df11946dbd50cabe5a7f7839`, priority revision 8. Selected conditional kappa remains .003125804. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19267611). The card is explicitly changed to an abstract signed-boundary side result; the physical-caller obligation is not claimed complete.

## Evidence

Before, the fixed-boundary theorem left variable productive credits outside its conclusion. After, the written dimension proof and two-dimensional table give a sharp counterexample to extending its no-coupling conclusion to every signed variable-boundary graph.

All local registered checks pass on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64:

- 305,721 complete ordered subspace triples over F2 in dimensions 0 through 4 and F3/F5 in dimension 2. Every equality case is checked. The binary RREF inventory is checked independently by closure under adjoining vectors.
- 64 explicit attaining constructions and 27 exact affine-envelope endpoint checks. Missing/spurious table rows, intersecting-plane equality and strict-threshold controls pass.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks take 0.240s and 0.247s respectively. These are timeout measurements, not a performance comparison; both are well below their 120s limits. Both VERIFY.json commands and the registered replay pass.
- At head `0821ba9ff3b55204042b007212f04d764b5d3921`, all seven committed files match working bytes; the declared base passes source-history ancestry. The official export passes integrity/input-coverage checks. Optimized replay passes in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all eight exported files keep their bytes and modes. Altered proof bytes, an altered count and a Boolean receipt mutation are rejected.
- The generated RESULT.json binds all six source files and records per-domain minima, minimizer counts and ordered trace hashes. No receipt was handwritten. No predecessor scientific computation was repeated.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/signed-triangle-tensor-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/signed-triangle-tensor-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/signed-triangle-tensor-gap
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/signed-triangle-tensor-gap --check-source-history
```

The marker is `PASS_SIGNED_TRIANGLE_TENSOR_GAP ordered_triples=305721 constructions=64 power_endpoint_checks=27`. A clean CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the exact local path; standard library only.

Canonical main, live open PRs, current claims and distinctive merged/main README searches were refreshed before committing. Cached overlap covered 317 open PRs and 5,857 Discussion records, with complete remote pagination; its sparse local search omitted 8,491 note paths, so separate searches used main's README tree. These are bounded overlap checks, not proof of novelty.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Only canonical subspace charts and the stated six-edge signed graph are optimized. The negative edges have no supplied realization as independent targets on arbitrary dirty inputs. A legal scalar contact graph, native phases, physical target delivery, restoration, ownership, adapters, movement, precision/tape, compiler closure, BIT and outer admission remain open and unpriced. The result does not change a paid supplier histogram or the selected frontier. The all-field conclusions rest on the written proof, not finite extrapolation. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run is claimed.

## Open next questions

- Realize this signed graph with a legal dirty-input scalar circuit, or prove a contact/path obstruction. First assign the three productive pairs to distinct logical lifetimes and charge every paid transition; independent target delivery and restoration are blockers.
- Determine the all-width optimum for 0<t<1, starting with unequal dimensions and nonzero intersections. The linear theorem and exact two-copy table do not resolve that optimization; a graph improvement would still need a complete physical invoice.

## Related open work

- [#6171](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6171) proves no tensor advantage with fixed repeated productive boundaries. This package changes that hypothesis and gives an exact signed graph gap; it does not dispute the theorem or compare a shared numerical optimum.
- [#4993](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4993) explores variable-boundary retiming on a particular carried-swap P104 graph. This package studies an abstract triangle of productive pairs and supplies no source-compatible word or competing P104 price.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one isolated research package. Seven files are added; shared code, frozen sources and selected-frontier records are unchanged.
